title: 2013 AMC 12B Problem 25
statement:
Let \(G\) be the set of polynomials of the form

\[ \begin{aligned} &P(z) = z^n + c_{n-1}z^{n-1} + \cdots \\ &\quad {}+ c_2 z^2 + c_1 z + 50, \end{aligned} \]

where \(c_1,\) \(c_2,\) \(\ldots,\) \(c_{n-1}\) are integers and \(P(z)\) has \(n\) distinct roots of the form \(a + ib\) with \(a\) and \(b\) integers. How many polynomials are in \(G?\)

solutions.text: Since the coefficients are real, nonreal roots occur in conjugate pairs, so \(P(z)\) factors into distinct linear factors \((z - c)\) with \(c \in \mathbb{Z}\) and quadratics \((z - (a+ib))(z - (a-ib))\) \(= z^2 - 2az + (a^2 + b^2).\) Each factor’s constant term divides \(50.\) For \(d=1,2,5,10,25,50,\) the numbers of conjugate pairs with \(a^2+b^2=d\) and \(b\ne0\) are \(1,2,4,4,5,6,\) respectively. Adding the two linear choices \(z-d,z+d\) gives \(|B_1|=3,\) \(|B_2|=4,\) \(|B_5|=6,\) \(|B_{10}|=6,\) \(|B_{25}|=7,\) and \(|B_{50}|=8.\) The factor-magnitude partitions of \(50\) using values greater than \(1\) are \(50,25\cdot2,10\cdot5,\) and \(5\cdot5\cdot2.\) Distinct roots require choosing two different \(B_5\) factors in the last case. Finally, account for the free presence of \(z+1\) and \(z^2+1\) (with \(z-1\) forced by the sign of the remaining product), gives \[ \begin{aligned} &2^2\left(8 + 7\cdot 4 + 6\cdot 6 + 4\binom{6}{2}\right) \\ &\quad = 4(8 + 28 + 36 + 60) = 528. \end{aligned} \] Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Real coefficients pair nonreal roots as conjugates, so \(P(z)\) factors into linear \((z - c)\) and quadratic \(z^2 - 2az + (a^2 + b^2)\) pieces, each with constant term dividing \(50\)
For each divisor \(d\) of \(50,\) count the basic factors of magnitude \(d\) (solutions of \(a^2 + b^2 = d,\) plus \(z \pm d\)), then multiply choices so the constant terms multiply to \(50\)
